text: Hello everyone, today we are going to move on to section B, grammar activity.In this period, we will focus on the two infinitives for modification.By the end of today's lesson, you are expected to deduce the rules of using two infinitives for modification.You also need to understand and use two infinitives for modification in context.Before class, please get your textbooks and worksheets ready.From the previous lessons, we've learned that people of different ages and cultures change the way they look for different reasons.Sometimes to look more beautiful, and sometimes to show social position or display group identity.Then how about animals?Are there any special reasons for the way they look?For example, why are polar bears white?Why do rabbits have long ears?And why do zebras have black and white stripes?Let's read the article on page 48 and find out.While reading, please answer the four questions in your worksheet and underline the evidence in the passage.You will have one minute.Welcome back!Let's check the answers together.The passage tells us that the way animals look is closely related to their survival.And to illustrate how animals' appearance helps them to avoid getting eaten, the author tells a story.What wild animals are mentioned in the story?Yes, a lioness and the zebras.At the beginning of the story, when the zebras are moving together across the grassland, a lioness is lying on a tree branch.Because she is waiting for her chance to attack.Then, as the zebras are getting nearer, the lioness is getting ready, because she knows something from her experience.What does she know?Right, she knows she will soon have a zebra to kill.Then why is she so confident?What makes it necessary for zebras to protect themselves by their stripes in the grassland?Yes, because there is no place to hide.However, lions are colorblind, so when zebras move in a large group, the lioness can only see a big mass of black and white stripes.So what problem does it cause to the lioness?Right, it's hard for her to see which zebra to attack.So the zebra's appearance does help them a lot.Then let's take a closer look at the answers.Have you noticed the two infinitives at the end of each sentence?What is the function of these two infinitives?Right, these two infinitives are used for modification, and each of them is used to modify a noun.For example, in the first answer, to attack is used to modify chance.And so are the rest of the examples.Then let's try to find some rules about how to use the two infinitives for modification from these sentences.Are the two infinitives used to modify subjects or objects?Do they come immediately before or after the nouns they modify?Have the actions they refer to being completed or not?You will have one minute to complete the grammar rules on page 49.So, two infinitives can be used to modify objects, and they come immediately after the nouns they modify.Such two infinitives refer to actions that have not been completed.Well done!Then, to help you better understand the rules, you are going to rewrite several sentences.Last term, we've learned to use relative clauses to modify nouns.Do you still remember?Can you use two infinitives instead?Let's take the first sentence as an example.We can also say she has a lot of work to do.In this sentence, the two infinitives is used to modify the noun work, and her work has not been completed yet.Now it's your turn to have a try.She has a lot of work that she should do.Please rewrite the next three sentences in your worksheet by using two infinitives.Have you finished?Let's check the answers.Sentence number two.Instead of using the relative clause that I need to write, we can also say I have an important report to write.Then in the third sentence, we can use to clean to replace the relative clause that he had to clean to modify the next room.The last one, we can just say there is nothing to eat in the fridge to express the same meaning of that we can eat.So what difference does it make when we use two infinitives instead of relative clauses?Yes, the sentences are more concise.Now I believe you have a better understanding of using two infinitives for modification.And besides two infinitives, what other forms can we use for modification?In book two, we've learned two other forms of verbs as the attributive.What are they?Yes, they are verb-ing forms and verb-ed forms.Then what are the differences of using these three forms of verbs for modification?Let's read a short paragraph about the experiment in education in book two unit two to refresh your memory.Please read a paragraph and underline the verb-ing and verb-ed forms as the attributive.在这个课程中,我们可以找到词词-ed的形式-set和-convert,用来改变-series和-farm,与其他类似。我们还可以找到词词-ing的形式-dealing with和-teaching,改变-teacher,与其他类似。在这个课程中,我们可以找到词词-ing和-ed的形式-set和-convert,用来改变-series和-farm,与其他类似。对,他们代表过去的行动。那么,词词-ing的形式,它们是怎么不同于词词-ed的形式呢?词词-ing的形式代表什么,或者是什么人在做,或者是在行动。它们通常有活动的意义。现在,让我们看看你们能否理解它们的分别。让我们试试用它们在一个课程中。请在49号的文章中填充正确的形式和词词。您将有2分钟。----------------------中文字幕提供
